SMTO-GWT-0052 — The Gateway computer refused SMTO's connection

GUID: ecd5ab38-1b0e-493c-a1b5-171fb7eed734
Slug: gateway-connection-refused
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • SMTO reached the Gateway's computer, but nothing there accepted the connection. Usually the Gateway program isn't running or the port number is wrong. This request was not sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the Gateway program is running on that computer. If the computer was restarted, start the Gateway again, or ask the person who manages it to. A refused connection most often means no Gateway is running there to answer.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Edit for this Gateway, and check that Port (8787 unless it was changed) and Scheme match how the Gateway was set up. With the wrong port, SMTO knocks on a door where no Gateway is waiting.
  3. If the Gateway computer has a firewall, ask its manager to allow connections to the Gateway's port from the computer running SMTO. Some firewalls turn connections away in exactly this way.
  4. Select Check connection for the Gateway. This makes a fresh connection and shows whether the Gateway now answers.

What success looks like

  • Check connection shows the Gateway as connected, and your request runs without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Before repeating an earlier step that was interrupted, check whether it already finished; a refused connection doesn't prove earlier work didn't run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Connecting to the selected inbound Gateway failed with ECONNREFUSED before the request was sent; either nothing is listening on that host and port or a firewall actively rejected the connection.

What this means

  • Connection setup returned ECONNREFUSED before the application request was sent. A listener absence or explicit network rejection is possible; the code does not distinguish them. This connection failure occurs before application request transmission. That boundary applies to this request and does not settle any previous operation.

Why this can happen

  • Connection setup returned ECONNREFUSED before the application request was sent. A listener absence or explicit network rejection is possible; the code does not distinguish them.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the configured endpoint with the intended Gateway listener and any explicit network rejection evidence.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, confirm the Gateway service is running and listening on the configured port (8787 by default; for example ss -ltnp), and that Scheme, Host and Port in the Gateway record match it. If it is listening, check host firewall rules that reject the Server's address. Earlier operations keep their own recorded outcome.
  • Check the configured Gateway host/port and whether its listener is running.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended listener accepts the connection and its verified identity matches the selection.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • This connection failure occurs before application request transmission. That boundary applies to this request and does not settle any previous operation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
